chapter.heading: 1 Corinthians 1
Greeting
chapter.v: 1 Paul,calledby the will of God to be an apostle of Christ Jesus, and our brother Sosthenes,

To the church of God that is in Corinth, to thosesanctified in Christ Jesus,called to be saints together with all those who in every placecall upon the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, both their Lord and ours:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
give thanks to my God always for you because of the grace of God that was given you in Christ Jesus,
that in every wayyou were enriched in him in all speech and all knowledge—
the testimony about Christ was confirmed among you—
wait for the revealing of our Lord Jesus Christ,
who will sustain you to the end,guiltless in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
God is faithful, by whom you were called into the fellowship of his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.
I appeal to you, brothers, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that all of you agree, and that there be nodivisions among you, but that you be united in the same mind and the same judgment.
quarreling among you, my brothers.
What I mean is thateach one of you says, “I follow Paul,” or “I followApollos,” or “I follow Cephas,” or “I follow Christ.”
Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?
I thank God that I baptized none of you exceptCrispus and Gaius,
so that no one may say that you were baptized in my name.
the household of Stephanas. Beyond that, I do not know whether I baptized anyone else.)
not with words of eloquent wisdom, lest the cross of Christ be emptied of its power.
the power of God.
and the discernment of the discerning I will thwart.”
Has not God made foolish the wisdom of the world?
For since, in the wisdom of God, the world did not know God through wisdom, it pleased God through the folly of what we preach to save those who believe.
Jews demand signs and Greeks seek wisdom,
crucified, a stumbling block to Jews and folly to Gentiles,
the wisdom of God.
For the foolishness of God is wiser than men, and the weakness of God is stronger than men.
not many of you were wise according to worldly standards, not many were powerful, not many were of noble birth.
God chose what is weak in the world to shame the strong;
bring to nothing things that are,
that no human being might boast in the presence of God.
redemption,
“Let the one who boasts, boast in the Lord.”

footnotes.footnote: 1:10 Or *brothers and sisters*. In New Testament usage, depending on the context, the plural Greek word *adelphoi* (translated “brothers”) may refer either to *brothers* or to *brothers and sisters*; also verses 11, 26
